name: Humanitarian funding gap
value: WFP cuts Gaza aid; Yemen appeal unmet
summary: WFP has cut Gaza food aid for lack of funds and IOM seeks $45m for Yemen's displaced; no large-scale suspension found
state: WFP cut monthly food assistance in Gaza by about 500,000 people in October because of funding shortages (Al Jazeera, 19 Oct; WFP). IOM said on 1 Nov it needs $45 million over six months for more than 300,000 people displaced in western Yemen (Khaleej Times). Major ration cuts meet Watch; no large-scale suspension of food or health aid in a famine-risk country was found as of 26 Nov.
for_you: UN agencies' appeals, listed on OCHA's Financial Tracking Service, show where funding gaps are largest.
rubric_hit: Major ration cuts announced = Watch; no large-scale pipeline break

sources.title: Al Jazeera — WFP cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza amid funding shortages
WFP — Funding cuts force WFP to drastically reduce lifesaving assistance in Gaza
Khaleej Times — More than 300,000 have fled fighting in western Yemen: UN

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
